title: Philip II of Macedon wins at Chaeronea
summary: Philip II of Macedon and his son Alexander defeated an alliance led by Athens and Thebes at Chaeronea in Boeotia.
reason: Macedon was expanding south, and Athens, urged on by Demosthenes, joined Thebes to stop Philip.
significance: The victory ended the independence of the Greek city states and gave Macedon control of Greece.

title: The Great Persecution of Christians begins
summary: On the feast of the Terminalia, imperial troops destroyed the new church at Nicomedia, and the next day an edict ordered churches and scriptures destroyed across the empire.
reason: Diocletian and his Caesar Galerius saw the growing Christian church as a threat to the unity and traditional religion of the empire.
significance: It was the last and most severe persecution of Christians in the Roman Empire.

title: Wu Zetian becomes China's only empress regnant
summary: Wu Zetian, who had long ruled through her husband and sons, took the throne in her own name and proclaimed a new Zhou dynasty. She ruled until 705.
reason: After decades of controlling the Tang court, she removed her son Emperor Ruizong and claimed full imperial authority.
significance: She remains the only woman in Chinese history to rule as emperor in her own right.

title: Zhao Kuangyin founds the Song dynasty
summary: After his troops proclaimed him emperor at Chen Bridge, the general Zhao Kuangyin took the throne from the child ruler of the Later Zhou and founded the Song dynasty.
reason: Northern China had suffered a series of short military regimes, and the army wanted a strong adult ruler.
significance: The Song reunified most of China and presided over a great age of commerce, technology and learning.

title: The Sicilian Vespers revolt against French rule
summary: At the hour of vespers on Easter Monday, the people of Palermo rose against the French soldiers of Charles of Anjou, and the revolt spread across Sicily.
reason: Sicilians resented heavy taxes and the harsh rule of the Angevin French.
significance: Sicily passed to the Crown of Aragon, starting a long war over southern Italy.

title: Hussites throw councillors from Prague's New Town Hall
summary: A crowd of Hussites led by the priest Jan Zelivsky stormed the New Town Hall in Prague and threw several town councillors out of the windows to their deaths.
reason: Anger had built since the execution of Jan Hus, and the councillors had refused to release imprisoned Hussites.
significance: It triggered the Hussite Wars, which lasted until the 1430s.
place: New Town Hall, Prague, Czech Republic

title: The Victoria completes the first circumnavigation
summary: The ship Victoria, commanded by Juan Sebastian Elcano, reached Sanlucar de Barrameda with 18 survivors, three years after Magellan's fleet of five ships had set out.
reason: The expedition had sought a western route to the Spice Islands, and the survivors returned westward around Africa.
significance: It was the first voyage around the world and proved the true size of the Earth's oceans.

title: Francis Xavier brings Christianity to Japan
summary: The Jesuit missionary Francis Xavier landed at Kagoshima with the Japanese convert Anjiro and began the first Christian mission in Japan.
reason: Xavier had met Anjiro in Malacca and hoped Japan would be fertile ground for conversion.
significance: It began the Christian century in Japan, which saw hundreds of thousands of converts before persecution.

title: Tokugawa Ieyasu becomes shogun of Japan
summary: Emperor Go-Yozei appointed Tokugawa Ieyasu as shogun, founding the Tokugawa shogunate with its seat at Edo.
reason: Ieyasu's victory at Sekigahara made him the dominant warlord, and the title gave his rule legitimacy.
significance: The Tokugawa shogunate ruled a unified and largely peaceful Japan until 1868.

title: Pope Urban VIII consecrates the new St. Peter's Basilica
summary: After 120 years of building, the new basilica of St. Peter in Rome, with Michelangelo's dome, was consecrated by Pope Urban VIII.
reason: The old Constantinian basilica was crumbling, and the popes wanted a church to express the glory of Rome.
significance: It became the largest church of its age and the central symbol of the Catholic Church.

title: Louis XIV revokes the Edict of Nantes
summary: With the Edict of Fontainebleau, Louis XIV outlawed Protestantism in France, ordering churches destroyed and pastors expelled.
reason: The king sought religious unity under Catholicism as part of his absolute rule.
significance: Some 200,000 Huguenots fled to Protestant countries, taking their skills and businesses with them.

title: England and Scotland unite as Great Britain
summary: The Acts of Union came into force, joining the kingdoms of England and Scotland into a single Kingdom of Great Britain with one parliament at Westminster.
reason: England wanted to secure the Protestant succession, and Scotland, hit by the failed Darien scheme, wanted access to English markets.
significance: It created the British state that became the center of a global empire.

title: East India Company wins the Battle of Buxar
summary: Company forces under Hector Munro defeated the combined armies of Mir Qasim, the Nawab of Awadh and the Mughal emperor Shah Alam II.
reason: Mir Qasim had tried to assert independence from the Company and allied with other Indian rulers against it.
significance: It confirmed Company supremacy in eastern India.

title: Russia, Prussia and Austria agree the First Partition of Poland
summary: Russia, Prussia and Austria signed agreements in Saint Petersburg to annex about a third of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth.
reason: The neighbouring powers wanted to keep a balance among themselves while exploiting the weakness of the Commonwealth.
significance: It began the process that erased Poland from the map by 1795.

title: Robespierre falls on 9 Thermidor
summary: The National Convention turned on Maximilien Robespierre and his allies, who were arrested and guillotined the next day.
reason: Deputies feared they would be the next victims of the Terror.
significance: It ended the Reign of Terror.

title: Chile forms its first national government junta
summary: An open council in Santiago replaced the Spanish governor with a junta.
reason: With the Spanish king captive, Chilean creoles chose self government in his name.
significance: It began Chile's road to independence and is its national day.

title: July Revolution breaks out in Paris
summary: Parisians built barricades and fought royal troops for three days, forcing Charles X to abdicate in favor of Louis Philippe.
reason: Charles X issued ordinances that suspended press freedom and dissolved the newly elected Chamber of Deputies.
significance: It ended the restored Bourbon line in France and inspired uprisings in Belgium, Poland and elsewhere.

title: Convention of Kanagawa opens Japan to American ships
summary: Japan and the United States signed a treaty opening the ports of Shimoda and Hakodate to American ships and allowing a consul in Japan.
reason: Perry returned with a larger fleet, and the shogunate concluded it could not resist Western naval power.
significance: It was Japan's first treaty with a Western power and led to similar treaties with other nations.

title: Mendel presents his laws of inheritance
summary: Gregor Mendel read the first part of his paper on pea plant hybridization to the Natural History Society of Brno, describing how traits are inherited in fixed ratios.
reason: Mendel had spent eight years crossing thousands of pea plants in his monastery garden to find the rules of heredity.
significance: Ignored for decades, his work became the foundation of genetics after its rediscovery in 1900.

title: Golden spike completes the first transcontinental railroad
summary: The tracks of the Central Pacific and Union Pacific railroads were joined with a ceremonial golden spike at Promontory Summit, Utah.
reason: Congress had backed the line with land grants and bonds to bind California to the rest of the Union and open the West.
significance: It cut the journey across the United States from months to about a week and transformed the West.

title: Max Planck presents the quantum hypothesis
summary: Max Planck presented his derivation of the law of black-body radiation to the German Physical Society in Berlin, assuming that energy is emitted in discrete packets, or quanta.
reason: Classical physics could not explain the measured spectrum of radiation from hot bodies, and Planck sought a formula that fit the experimental data.
significance: The talk is regarded as the birth of quantum theory, which reshaped physics and modern technology.

title: Gandhi launches satyagraha in Johannesburg
summary: At a mass meeting of Indians in the Empire Theatre in Johannesburg, Mohandas Gandhi led a pledge to resist a discriminatory registration law through nonviolent disobedience.
reason: The Transvaal government had proposed an ordinance forcing all Indians to register and carry passes.
significance: It began the method of nonviolent resistance Gandhi later used in India and that inspired civil rights movements worldwide.

title: Roald Amundsen reaches the South Pole
summary: A Norwegian party of five led by Roald Amundsen reached the South Pole using dog sledges, five weeks ahead of Robert Falcon Scott's British expedition.
reason: Amundsen changed his plans from the North Pole after hearing it had been claimed, and raced Scott to the south.
significance: It was the first human arrival at the South Pole, a peak of the heroic age of polar exploration.

title: Germany releases poison gas at Ypres
summary: German troops released chlorine gas against French and colonial troops near Ypres, opening the Second Battle of Ypres with the first large-scale use of poison gas on the Western Front.
reason: Germany sought a way to break the stalemate of trench warfare.
significance: It introduced chemical warfare on a mass scale, later banned by the Geneva Protocol.

title: Chiang Kai-shek launches the Northern Expedition
summary: The National Revolutionary Army under Chiang Kai-shek set out from Guangzhou on a military campaign to defeat the warlords and unify China.
reason: The Kuomintang, allied with the Communists and Soviet advisers, aimed to end warlord rule over most of China.
significance: It brought China under nominal Nationalist rule by 1928 and ended the Beiyang government.

title: The Chinese Red Army begins the Long March
summary: Encircled by Nationalist forces, about 86,000 troops of the Red Army broke out of the Jiangxi Soviet and began a retreat of thousands of kilometers.
reason: Chiang Kai-shek's encirclement campaigns had made the Communist base in Jiangxi untenable.
significance: It saved the Chinese Communist Party and brought Mao Zedong to its leadership.

title: Germany annexes Austria in the Anschluss
summary: German troops crossed into Austria unopposed, and Hitler announced its union with Germany the next day.
reason: Hitler wanted to unite all Germans in one Reich, and he moved to stop Chancellor Schuschnigg's referendum on independence.
significance: It was Hitler's first annexation of a sovereign state and showed the Western powers would not resist.

title: Soviet Union attacks Finland, starting the Winter War
summary: Soviet troops crossed the Finnish border and Soviet planes bombed Helsinki. The Finns held out through the winter with fierce resistance before agreeing to peace in March 1940.
reason: Stalin demanded Finnish territory near Leningrad and bases on the Gulf of Finland, and Finland refused.
significance: Finland kept its independence but lost Karelia, and the poor Soviet performance encouraged Hitler to think the Red Army was weak.
place: Helsinki and the Karelian Isthmus, Finland

title: Japan invades northern French Indochina
summary: Japanese troops crossed from China into northern Vietnam and fought brief battles with French colonial forces around Lang Son before Vichy France accepted Japanese bases.
reason: Japan wanted to cut the supply route to Nationalist China through Haiphong and to gain a foothold in South-East Asia after France's defeat.
significance: It drew US economic sanctions on Japan and began the Japanese presence in Indochina that later fed the Vietnamese independence struggle.

title: Britain and the Soviet Union invade Iran
summary: British and Soviet forces entered Iran from the south and north and overcame its army within days. Reza Shah was forced to abdicate in favour of his son Mohammad Reza Pahlavi.
reason: The Allies wanted Iran's oil fields and a supply route to the Soviet Union, and distrusted the Shah's ties to Germany.
significance: The Persian Corridor became a key Lend-Lease route, and the occupation deeply shaped Iranian nationalism.

title: Axis forces in North Africa surrender in Tunisia
summary: The last German and Italian forces in Tunisia surrendered to the Allies, and about 250,000 soldiers became prisoners.
reason: Squeezed between the British advancing from Libya and the Americans and British from Algeria, the Axis armies had no way to escape by sea.
significance: It ended the North African campaign and opened the way for the invasion of Italy.

title: Setif massacre begins in French Algeria
summary: A victory parade in Setif turned violent when police tried to seize Algerian nationalist flags, and riots killed about a hundred Europeans. French forces and settler militias then killed thousands of Algerians in reprisals over the following weeks.
reason: Algerian nationalists hoped the Allied victory would bring freedom, while the colonial authorities were determined to suppress them.
significance: It radicalised Algerian nationalism and is seen as a prelude to the Algerian War of Independence.

title: Britain declares an emergency in Kenya
summary: The colonial governor declared a state of emergency in Kenya and arrested Jomo Kenyatta and other nationalist leaders.
reason: The Mau Mau movement among the Kikuyu was attacking settlers and loyalists over land and colonial rule.
significance: The brutal counterinsurgency that followed hastened the end of British rule in East Africa.

title: Geneva Accords divide Vietnam
summary: The Geneva Conference ended with agreements that divided Vietnam at the 17th parallel and confirmed the independence of Laos and Cambodia.
reason: France wanted out of Indochina after Dien Bien Phu, and the great powers sought a settlement.
significance: The temporary division of Vietnam led to the Vietnam War.

title: The Cuban Missile Crisis begins
summary: President Kennedy was shown photographs proving that the Soviet Union was building nuclear missile sites in Cuba. Thirteen days of confrontation followed.
reason: Khrushchev placed missiles in Cuba to protect Castro and offset American missiles near the Soviet Union.
significance: It was the closest the world came to nuclear war.
place: White House, Washington, D.C., United States

title: Israel strikes Egypt, starting the Six-Day War
summary: Israel launched surprise air strikes that destroyed most of Egypt's air force on the ground, then fought Egypt, Jordan and Syria.
reason: Egypt had expelled UN peacekeepers, closed the Straits of Tiran and massed troops in Sinai.
significance: Israel captured Sinai, Gaza, the West Bank, East Jerusalem and the Golan Heights, reshaping the conflict.

title: Nixon and Brezhnev sign the SALT I agreements
summary: In Moscow, Nixon and Leonid Brezhnev signed the Anti-Ballistic Missile Treaty and an interim agreement limiting strategic missiles.
reason: Both powers wanted to slow the costly arms race in an era of detente.
significance: It was the first agreement to limit American and Soviet strategic weapons.

title: Viking 1 lands on Mars
summary: NASA's Viking 1 lander touched down on Mars and sent back the first photographs from the planet's surface.
reason: NASA wanted to study Mars and search for signs of life.
significance: It was the first fully successful landing on Mars.

title: Reagan and Gorbachev sign the INF Treaty
summary: At the White House, Reagan and Gorbachev signed a treaty eliminating all American and Soviet intermediate range nuclear missiles.
reason: The deployment of missiles in Europe in the early 1980s had alarmed both sides.
significance: It was the first treaty to abolish a whole class of nuclear weapons.
place: White House, Washington, D.C., United States

title: Operation Desert Storm begins
summary: A US-led coalition began a massive air campaign against Iraqi forces in Iraq and Kuwait.
reason: Iraq ignored a United Nations deadline of 15 January to withdraw from Kuwait.
significance: It showed the power of precision weapons and led to Kuwait's liberation within weeks.

title: Nelson Mandela becomes president of South Africa
summary: Nelson Mandela was sworn in as South Africa's first black president at the Union Buildings in Pretoria.
reason: The ANC won the country's first elections with universal suffrage in April 1994.
significance: It marked the formal end of apartheid.

title: September 11 attacks
summary: Al-Qaeda hijackers flew airliners into the World Trade Center and the Pentagon, and a fourth plane crashed in Pennsylvania. Nearly 3,000 people died.
reason: Osama bin Laden sought to punish the United States for its Middle East policies and provoke a wider war.
significance: It led to the war on terror, the invasions of Afghanistan and Iraq, and a new security era.
place: World Trade Center, New York City, United States

title: US-led invasion of Iraq begins
summary: American, British and allied forces began air strikes and a ground invasion of Iraq.
reason: The US accused Saddam Hussein of hiding weapons of mass destruction and links to terrorism, claims later shown false.
significance: It toppled Saddam but led to years of insurgency and sectarian war.

title: Tunisian revolution begins
summary: Street vendor Mohamed Bouazizi set himself on fire in Sidi Bouzid, sparking protests that toppled President Ben Ali within a month.
reason: Unemployment, corruption and police abuse had built deep frustration.
significance: It ignited the Arab Spring across the Middle East and North Africa.

title: Typhoon Haiyan strikes the Philippines
summary: One of the strongest tropical cyclones ever recorded at landfall hit the central Philippines, killing over 6,000 people, mostly in Tacloban.
reason: The storm surge swept across low coasts of Leyte and Samar.
significance: It became a symbol of climate vulnerability in poor countries.

title: AlphaFold solves protein structure prediction
summary: The organisers of the CASP14 competition announced that DeepMind's AlphaFold predicted protein structures almost as accurately as experiments.
reason: Predicting a protein's shape from its amino acids had been a 50-year challenge in biology.
significance: It transformed biology and won the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
